predecessors.note: 'Created sometime before 970, it was broken off the larger March of Carinthia'; in 976 it was placed under the jurisdiction of the new Duchy of Carinthia. Its lands had been Carantanian, then Bavarian-suzerain (c. 740), East Frankish (843), overrun by the Magyars after 907 and reconquered up to the Lafnitz after the Lechfeld of 955. [Reviewer eu-08-x, 2026-10-25: predecessor corrected from duchy-of-carinthia (founded 976) to the Bavarian duchy, whose March of Carinthia the march was broken off before 970] Bavaria's years 970-976 are the vassal pair in the ledger (repair of 2026-10-25).

sources.title: Duchy of Styria
sources.note: 1180 duchy created by Barbarossa from the March of Styria; 1186 Georgenberg Pact; 1192 inheritance by the Babenbergs; 1246 extinction; silent on Pitten (1158), the Traungau and Steyr; read for the thin finding.

notes:
One page opened (budget 2-5; thin). The March of Styria page has no infobox and no area. The Bavaria pages (Duchy of Bavaria, Otto I of Bavaria) say 'Styria was separated from Bavaria in 1180'; this page puts the march under Carinthia from 976 and gives the Otakars as its margraves with no Bavarian suzerainty, so the Bavaria dossier leaves Styria out of its shape and records 1180 as a caption. Not settled: the exact start (before 970), when the Otakars became effectively independent of Carinthia (the ledger keeps the vassal tint in duchy-of-carinthia until 1180), the eastern border after 1043 (Hungary's side), the capital (Steyr is a guess from 'Margraves of Steyr' 1074 and is not given), and the personal union with Austria after 1192 (duchy-of-styria, eu-09).

Repair of 2026-10-25 (review findings): (1) the overlord pairs are added from the vassal's side: Bavaria 970-976 and Carinthia 976-1180 (mirrors of stem-duchy-of-bavaria 970/976 and duchy-of-carinthia 976/1180). The March of Styria page (re-read) gives 'before 970' for the creation as a Bavarian march broken off the Carinthian march, 976 for the transfer to the new Duchy of Carinthia, and 'gradually gained independence from the Carinthian dukes' with no year; the 1180 end of the tint follows the page's 'Imperial State in its own right' date. (2) Thin finding: the Duchy of Styria page (opened) and the March of Styria page are both silent on the Otakar acquisitions (the Pitten inheritance of 1158 and the Traungau): neither names Pitten in 1158 or the Traungau or Steyr as lands joined to Styria, so they are not drawn (the 1042/43 land 'up to Pitten and the Leitha' is already drawn); two pages are now used of the 2-5 budget. (3) The 1042 circle (16.0 E 47.7 N, 45 km) overlaps about 15 of the 78 cells of Lower Austria that margraviate-of-austria also draws; it was not changed because the review did not flag it (the circle is a coarse reading of 'east of the Mur up to Pitten and the Leitha').
